PRE-DRAFT — Firefox Desktop MAU through 2027, on real Glean telemetry

The headline 2027 desktop forecast: raw daily MAU on 2027-12-15, trained on the real Glean desktop telemetry we have (2025-05-22 → 2026-10-09, 17 months), with the model re-tuned for a short history and one correction (Linux automated traffic) applied because the forecast was implausible without it. Everything else in the data is left as it is, by design: this is what the data we actually have produces. The forecast trained on the simulated (Glean-equivalent) history is kept as the validation build (REPORT_build5_glean_equivalent.html); the two agree once the Linux correction is accounted for (§3).

Read the world number, not the split. mozaic reconciles tiles top-down, so a Linux-only correction moved the Windows and Mac forecasts too; the per-OS figures are indicative. The world total is 161,546,764 on 2027-12-15 (-2.9% from 166,290,298 on 2026-12-15), of which 4,212,828 is the Linux automated-traffic level held flat (§2); the forecast for everyone else is 157,333,936.

2. How it was built

  • Data. glean_telemetry.active_users_aggregates, Firefox Desktop, MAU by country × OS (15 markets + ROW; Windows / Mac / Linux), 2025-05-22 → 2026-10-09. No simulated history. The 2025 Legacy-outage mask used by the validation build is off (real Glean has no outage). The Iran shutdown crater (March–May 2026) is filled for fitting with the counterfactual built for the validation build; the fill's DAU scale is within 1% of real Glean, the only borrowed input.
  • Model. mozaic (Prophet per tile, top-down reconciliation) with the October 2026 desktop lock, except the settings that govern how freely the trend may bend: additive seasonality regime, changepoint prior scale 0.005, 3 changepoints, changepoint range 0.8 (lock: multiplicative, 0.1649, 40, 0.87). The lock is tuned for five-plus years of history; on 17 months it read the one autumn ramp it saw as trend and sent MAU up and to the right while the data trend is down (world −3.8% YoY). Three probe rounds (COMPARISONS.html §3) found the additive, near-linear setting is a stable region; the centre was taken. Config cps0.005_thresh032_recent17_cpr0.8_ncp3_clip0.6_sps0.00825_regimeadditive.
  • Linux automated traffic (code b). Measured from real Glean client data, not from any reference series: a client counts as automated on a day if its ISP's share of "first seen inside the 28-day window with at most two active days" is ≥ 0.8. Hosting and cloud providers (Hetzner, Aruba Networks, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle, Tencent, …) come out at 0.95–1.00, residential ISPs about 0.3. The component is 4,212,828 MAU over the last 28 days of history (23% of Linux MAU; ROW 43%, DE 27%, US 25%), against a 0.4–0.7M baseline through 2025. It is subtracted from the Linux training rows before the model runs, so the surge is not learned as trend, and added back held flat at the last-28-day level: a no-growth planning assumption (Brendan, 2026-10-14), in a series that has only grown, in a term the 2027 KPI may or may not count. Windows (0.2% of MAU) and Mac (~0) are not corrected. Alternatives: zero (−4,212,828), growth (open).
  • China. The June 2026 MozillaOnline migration step is handled as in the validation build (measured curve subtracted and added back, Windows/Mac, code o).

3. Check against the validation build

With the Linux component removed, this forecast gives 157,333,936 on 2027-12-15; the validation build, trained on 6.8 years of simulated history with a different model configuration, gives 157,222,571. Two histories, two configurations, the same number once the one measured short component is accounted for. That agreement, not the tuning itself, is the justification for the re-tuned parameters: they were chosen by inspection, and an inspected choice needs an independent check.

Dotted orange is this forecast minus its own Linux add-back; green is the validation build. Blue is this build without the Linux correction (Linux to 21.9M, growing without bound in the multiplicative runs). Full detail, including the first run with the locked configuration (world MAU 169M → 229M, unusable), is in COMPARISONS.html.

4. How far off could it be

No backtest is possible on 17 months. By analogy, the validation build's configuration run from eight past dates on the long history missed the following year by 7% or less half the time and 10% or less nine times in ten at this horizon (median signed error -3.1%, i.e. it ran low). Around 161,546,764 that is ±10,851,370 to ±16,047,567; treat it as a floor, since this build has less history. Two further ranges:

The parameter neighbourhood spans about ±1.6M. The Linux path spans 157,333,936 (fleet vanishes) to 161,546,764 (held flat) and higher if it keeps growing.

5. Known limitations, deliberately left in

  • The January 2027 dip is an artifact. Real MAU fell 13M between mid-December 2025 and mid-January 2026; about 8M of that was Firefox 148 fixing duplicate client ids. With one observed year the model reads it as seasonal and repeats it in January 2027. It does not affect December 15. A corrected twin is planned as a secondary comparison, not as the headline (the real data stays uncorrected except where the forecast is implausible).
  • Published-Glean units. The number includes the remaining duplicate-id inflation (about 1% of Windows MAU, shrinking) and the Linux automated traffic. The validation build's units (glean_equivalent) exclude both, which is why its 157.2M is compared with this build's non-bot 157,333,936, not with 161,546,764.
  • One observed year of seasonality. Shape within the year is weaker than in the validation build; the Dec-15 point is anchored by the near-linear trend.
  • Seam step −1.49% on the 7-day means at 2026-10-10: the Linux component's October spike sits above its 28-day mean, so the first forecast days sit below the last actuals. Reported, not smoothed.
  • MAU only. DAU for this build has not been run (Brendan, 2026-10-13: MAU only); the validation build carries DAU.
